title: Does Federated Training Degrade Explainability? A Comparative Analysis of Grad-CAM Faithfulness in Centralized vs. Federated Deepfake Detection
abstract: arXiv:2610.39483v1 Announce Type: new  Abstract: Automated detection has become the essential safeguard against realistic synthetic media, but deploying it at scale requires training on sensitive data from multiple organizations, putting privacy and the transparency demanded by forensic review in direct conflict. Federated learning resolves the privacy side by sharing only model updates rather than raw data, but whether this comes at the cost of trustworthy gradient-based explanations, which analysts rely on to decide whether or not to trust a flagged clip, has not been studied. We present the systematic study of Grad-CAM explanation faithfulness under federated deepfake detection, evaluating an EfficientNet-B4 detector on FaceForensics++ across five federated clients under varying degrees of data heterogeneity. We find that the relationship between federation and explanation quality is non-monotonic: at near-IID (Independent and Identically Distributed Data) and moderate heterogeneity

translated_title: 联邦训练会降低可解释性吗？集中式与联邦式深度伪造检测中Grad-CAM忠实度的对比分析
translated_abstract: 自动化检测已成为对抗逼真合成媒体的关键保障，但其大规模部署需要使用来自多个组织的敏感数据进行训练，这使得隐私保护与取证审查所要求的透明度产生了直接冲突。联邦学习通过仅共享模型更新而非原始数据的方式解决了隐私问题，但这是否会以牺牲可信的基于梯度的解释为代价——而分析师正是依赖这些解释来判断是否信任被标记的片段——这一问题尚未被研究。我们对联邦深度伪造检测下的Grad-CAM解释忠实度进行了系统性研究，在不同程度的数据异构性条件下，使用EfficientNet-B4检测器在FaceForensics++数据集上对五个联邦客户端进行评估。我们发现联邦化与解释质量之间的关系是非单调的：在接近IID（独立同分布）和中等异构性条件下
tldr: 本文首次系统研究了联邦学习对深度伪造检测模型Grad-CAM解释忠实度的影响，发现联邦化与解释质量之间呈非单调关系，为隐私保护与法证可解释性之间的权衡提供了重要依据。
en_tdlr: This paper presents the first systematic study of Grad-CAM explanation faithfulness in federated deepfake detection, revealing a non-monotonic relationship between federation and explanation quality, providing key insights into the trade-off between privacy protection and forensic explainability.
